learnings: Short-term (5-day holds), best in both 2020-23 and 2024-25: Uptrend + RSI(2) < 10 / downtrend + RSI(2) > 90 (short, 5d) median Sharpe 0.13 then 0.55, win 64% in 2024-25; Close 5% below / above the 9-day MA (long, 5d) median Sharpe 0.10 then 0.08, win 51% in 2024-25; Uptrend + close back above 9-day MA after a dip / mirror (long, 5d) median Sharpe 0.20 then 0.05, win 54% in 2024-25; 20-day EMA crosses 50-day EMA (short, 5d) median Sharpe 0.02 then 0.48, win 53% in 2024-25.

Short-term (5-day holds) that worked over 2007-2026 but failed in 2024-25: MACD cross with the 200-day trend (long, 5d) full 0.13 vs 2024-25 -0.79; 55-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 5d) full 0.15 vs 2024-25 -0.16.

Long-term (10-40 day holds), best in both 2020-23 and 2024-25: Uptrend + close back above 9-day MA after a dip / mirror (long, 20d) median Sharpe 0.30 then 0.44, win 57% in 2024-25; Bullish / bearish MACD-histogram divergence (long, 40d) median Sharpe 0.32 then 0.25, win 49% in 2024-25; Uptrend pullback to the 20-day MA / downtrend rally to it (long, 20d) median Sharpe 0.18 then 0.27, win 47% in 2024-25; 20-day EMA crosses 50-day EMA (short, 40d) median Sharpe 0.15 then 0.36, win 57% in 2024-25.

Long-term (10-40 day holds) that worked over 2007-2026 but failed in 2024-25: 20-day EMA crosses 50-day EMA (long, 40d) full 0.16 vs 2024-25 -1.32; 55-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 40d) full 0.16 vs 2024-25 -0.90; MACD crosses above / below its signal (long, 40d) full 0.11 vs 2024-25 -0.70.

By family, median Sharpe 2007-18 → 2020-23 → 2024-25: Mean reversion + trend short-term +0.01 → -0.10 → +0.46; Mean reversion + trend long-term -0.04 → -0.00 → +0.17; Mean reversion short-term -0.18 → -0.21 → +0.07; Pullback in trend long-term -0.00 → +0.03 → +0.04; Crossover long-term +0.01 → -0.01 → +0.03; Divergence long-term -0.13 → -0.17 → +0.01; Pullback in trend short-term -0.04 → -0.15 → -0.02; Mean reversion long-term -0.11 → -0.17 → -0.05; Crossover + trend long-term +0.04 → +0.15 → -0.09; Divergence short-term -0.12 → -0.17 → -0.11; Breakout short-term +0.08 → +0.03 → -0.19; Breakout long-term +0.08 → +0.15 → -0.23; Crossover short-term -0.08 → -0.11 → -0.26; Crossover + trend short-term +0.06 → +0.04 → -0.54.

After a close 3% below the 9-day MA (2826 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 6 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 50% of the time; average drawdown before that -3.9% (worst -27%), return after 10 days +0.00% (up 50% of the time).

After a close 5% below the 9-day MA (1015 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 6 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 42% of the time; average drawdown before that -4.9% (worst -28%), return after 10 days +0.04% (up 50% of the time).

After a close 7% below the 9-day MA (389 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 7 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 37% of the time; average drawdown before that -6.1% (worst -28%), return after 10 days -0.24% (up 46% of the time).

After a close 10% below the 9-day MA (76 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 97% of cases (median 6 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 45% of the time; average drawdown before that -6.6% (worst -30%), return after 10 days +5.05% (up 64% of the time).
First dip to the 9-day MA in an uptrend (2332 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 52%, closed below the 50-day 69%, average dip -4.4%, return after 20 days +0.09% (up 51%).
First dip to the 20-day MA in an uptrend (1568 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 46%, closed below the 50-day 75%, average dip -4.2%, return after 20 days +0.29% (up 52%).
First dip to the 50-day MA in an uptrend (975 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 32%, closed below the 50-day 96%, average dip -4.7%, return after 20 days -0.28% (up 48%).
4408 rule x market x holding-period tests: a t-stat around 4.1 is what the luckiest test would show by chance, so prefer rules that work across many markets and in both 2007-18 and 2019+.
